articles.title: Nestle India declares special dividend of Rs 2. Check record date and other details
articles.content: Nestle India, the maker of Maggi noodles, has announced a special dividend of Rs 2 per equity share, payable on July 30, 2026. This payout will be funded by retained earnings. articles.title: Rupee clings to modest gains hemmed in by softer dollar, corporate hedging
articles.content: The Indian rupee saw a slight gain on Friday, though it's set for a weekly dip. Despite a weaker dollar and positive Asian currency movements, corporate demand and hedging activities are capping the rupee's rise. Analysts suggest the Federal Reserve's reduced urgency for rate hikes offers some comfort. Meanwhile, foreign investors are boosting Indian bond purchases ahead of index inclusion, while equities followed regional trends.

articles.title: Union Bank of India shares drop 5% post Q1 business update, global business decline marginally on quarterly basis

articles.title: Hitachi Energy, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, other power equipment stocks crash up to 10%. Here’s why
articles.content: Indian power sector stocks plunged Friday as reports emerged of a two-year exemption granted to four Chinese electrical equipment firms for government tenders. This move, aimed at easing project delays, allows companies like TBEA Energy and Nanjing Electric India to participate, despite earlier restrictions following the 2020 border clash. The exemption, however, is not to be treated as a precedent.

articles.title: AI bubble or boom? Why Warren Buffett called Big Short fame Michael Burry ‘Cassandra’
articles.content: Legendary investor Warren Buffett once dubbed Michael Burry, famous for predicting the 2008 housing crisis, as 'Cassandra' for his accurate but initially ignored warnings. Now, Burry is sounding the alarm on a potential AI bubble, citing massive tech spending and rising debt. He sees parallels to the Dotcom crash, suggesting current market optimism might be detached from economic reality, leading him to place bearish bets on several major companies.

articles.title: Forget Nifty50, smallcap index soars up to 200% in 2026. Will the mammoth rally continue?
articles.content: Indian smallcap stocks are outperforming the Nifty 50, with some indices soaring up to 200% this year. This rally is fueled by improving earnings, strong domestic liquidity, and renewed investor interest in bottom-up stock picking. While some experts see continued growth potential, others caution about rising valuations and suggest large-caps may offer better value. The sustainability of this trend hinges on earnings growth and easing geopolitical risks.

articles.title: Why India's hospital chains are racing to buy, not build, in Tier II and Tier III cities
articles.content: India's private hospitals are consolidating, shifting from building new facilities to acquiring existing ones. This trend, fueled by a decade of private equity funding, aims to address a critical shortage of beds, particularly outside major metros. While acquisitions offer faster growth, strategic assessment of regions is key. Experts predict this consolidation will continue, with tier II and III cities becoming the next growth frontier for healthcare infrastructure.

articles.title: US Stock market: Fed's Daly says AI, inflation uncertainty clouds interest rate outlook
articles.content: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly highlighted that US monetary policy remains slightly restrictive, but the economic outlook is increasingly uncertain.  The surge in AI-driven investment and a strong job market are creating complex dynamics.  While inflation could persist, slowing growth is also a possibility.  Daly stressed the need for careful evaluation of data before any interest rate adjustments.
